Proceed with protein quantification or store for downstream applications (-80 °C). Note: Suitable assays for protein quantification will depend on the composition of the final buffer in which the sample is dissolved. For example, the standard Bradford assay is incompatible with detergents (e.g., 1% SDS or Laemmli buffer), while the BCA assay is incompatible with reducing agents (e.g., DTT or 2-mercaptoethanol). The Bio-Rad’s detergent-compatible Bradford assay is compatible with moderate concentrations of detergent and reducing agent.

steps.title: Stabilize ex vivo tissue
steps.instruction: Place tissue sections into a labeled 1.5 mL centrifuge tube containing 300 µL pre‑chilled RNA later, store at 4 °C for at least overnight, then aspirate off the RNA later and proceed immediately to homogenization or store at –20 °C or below.

steps.title: Stabilize frozen tissue
steps.instruction: Place frozen tissue sections into a labeled 1.5 mL centrifuge tube containing 300 µL pre‑chilled RNA later‑ICE, incubate at –20 °C for at least 16 h, keep in RNA later‑ICE at –20 °C (or below) for storage, and when ready aspirate off the RNA later‑ICE and proceed to homogenization (samples remain stable in RNA later‑ICE for up to 30 min at room temperature).

steps.title: Lyse cultured THP‑1 cells
steps.instruction: Collect up to 5 × 10⁶ THP‑1 cells by centrifugation, remove residual medium/PBS, add 350 µL TRK lysis buffer supplemented with 2 % β‑mercaptoethanol, mix thoroughly and incubate at room temperature for 5 min, then add an equal volume of 70 % ethanol and continue to the RNA‑extraction section.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue in lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Weigh tissue (optional) in a homogenizer tube, add a 5 mm stainless‑steel bead and 350 µL TRK lysis buffer with 2 % β‑mercaptoethanol (pre‑chilled at 4 °C for ≥30 min), then homogenize in a QIAGEN TissueLyser II for 10 min at 25 Hz until fully homogenized (repeat if necessary).

steps.title: Centrifuge homogenate
steps.instruction: Transfer the homogenate to a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube and centrifuge at 12 000 g for 5 min at 4 °C to pellet debris; transfer the clear supernatant to a new pre‑labeled tube (perform a second spin if the supernatant is difficult to aspirate).

steps.title: Add ethanol to supernatant
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chilled 70 % ethanol to the collected supernatant (final volume ≈ 700 µL) and mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Bind RNA to column
steps.instruction: Transfer the entire mixture (≈ 700 µL, including any precipitate) to an RNA‑extraction spin column placed in a collection tube and centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 1 min at 4 °C; retain the flow‑through for protein extraction.

steps.title: Wash column with buffer I
steps.instruction: Move the column to a new 2 mL collection tube, add 500 µL wash buffer I (pre‑chilled ≥30 min), and centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 30 s at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash column with buffer II
steps.instruction: Discard the flow‑through, add 500 µL wash buffer II (pre‑chilled), centrifuge at 10 000 × g for 1 min at 4 °C; repeat this wash once more.

steps.title: Dry spin column membrane
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the spin column at ≥14 000 × g for 2 min at 4 °C in a clean 2 mL collection tube to dry the membrane.

steps.title: Elute RNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the column to a 1.5 mL tube, add 20–40 µL RNase‑free water to the membrane, centrifuge at maximum speed for 2 min at 4 °C; optionally repeat the elution by adding the eluate back to the membrane and centrifuging again for 2 min.

steps.title: Quantify or store RNA
steps.instruction: Place the tube containing the eluted RNA on ice, measure concentration with a NanoDrop spectrophotometer, or store the RNA at –80 °C.

steps.title: Precipitate protein from flowthrough
steps.instruction: Transfer the flow‑through collected in step 7 to a labeled 1.5 mL tube, add an equal volume of ice‑cold 100 % ethanol, invert or vortex until homogeneous, then store upright at –20 °C for ≥1 h (or overnight).

steps.title: First ethanol wash of protein pellet
steps.instruction: Briefly vortex the chilled tube for 2–3 s to break up large precipitate chunks, centrifuge at 2 000 × g for 3 min at 4 °C, carefully decant most supernatant leaving a small volume, and fully resuspend the pellet in 500 µL ice‑cold 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash and dry pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 2 000 × g for 3 min at 4 °C, resuspend the pellet again in 500 µL ice‑cold 70 % ethanol, centrifuge at 5 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, remove as much supernatant as possible, and allow residual ethanol to evaporate by air‑drying or using a vacuum aspirator (do not touch the pellet; avoid over‑drying and do not use a Speed‑vac).

steps.title: Dissolve protein pellet
steps.instruction: Dissolve the dried pellet in an appropriate downstream buffer (e.g., 1× Laemmli buffer with DTT), applying heat and/or vortexing as needed to achieve complete solubilisation.

steps.title: Quantify or store protein
steps.instruction: Perform protein quantification using a compatible assay (e.g., detergent‑compatible Bradford or BCA depending on buffer composition) or store the protein solution at –80 °C for later use.
